requirements.title: AI literacy of staff
requirements.guidanceText: Take measures so that the people who build or use your AI, including contractors working on your behalf, understand what it does and where it can go wrong. Since the 2026 amendment the law asks for suitable measures (for example a short training or briefing), not a fixed level for each person. This applies to every AI system, whatever its risk level. Keep a short record of who was trained and when.

requirements.title: Risk management system
requirements.guidanceText: For high-risk AI, run a risk management process across the whole life of the system. Identify the risks to health, safety and rights, decide how you reduce them, and review it regularly. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.

requirements.title: Data and data governance
requirements.guidanceText: Use training and test data that is relevant and as free of errors and bias as reasonably possible. Write down where the data came from and how you checked its quality. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.

requirements.title: Technical documentation
requirements.guidanceText: Keep technical documentation that shows how the system was built and tested, so an authority could check that it meets the rules. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.
requirements.lawReferenceLabel: AI Act Art. 11 and Annex IV

requirements.title: Transparency for users
requirements.guidanceText: Give the people who operate the system clear instructions: what it does, its limits, and how to read its output. Make sure they can understand the results. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.

requirements.title: Human oversight
requirements.guidanceText: A person must be able to understand, watch over, and if needed stop or override the AI. Decide who that person is and how they can intervene. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.

requirements.title: Accuracy, robustness and security
requirements.guidanceText: Test that the system is accurate and stable enough for its purpose, and protect it against errors, misuse, and attacks. Record your test results. High-risk deadline: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III; 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I.

requirements.title: Transparency about AI use
requirements.guidanceText: Tell people when they are interacting with an AI, and clearly label AI-generated or manipulated content such as chatbots, synthetic media, and deepfakes. Applies since 2 August 2026. For systems placed on the market before that date, machine-readable marking of AI-generated content (Art. 50(2)) is required from 2 December 2026.

templates.name: AI Governance Baseline
templates.description: Foundational steps every organisation using AI should complete, whatever the risk level.

items.title: Record the AI system in your inventory
items.guidanceText: Describe what this AI system is, what it is used for, and who is responsible for it inside your company.

items.title: Confirm staff AI literacy and training
items.guidanceText: Note what training the people building or using this system have had, so they understand its abilities and limits.

items.title: Document transparency toward affected people
items.guidanceText: Explain how you tell people they are dealing with AI, and how you label AI-generated content.

templates.name: AI Risk Assessment
templates.description: Write down the risks this AI creates and how you reduce them. This is your core documentation.

items.title: Describe the intended purpose and context
items.guidanceText: What is the system meant to do, who uses it, and who is affected by its decisions?

items.title: Identify risks to health, safety and rights
items.guidanceText: List the things that could go wrong for people, for example unfair outcomes, errors, or safety issues.

items.title: Describe your risk mitigation measures
items.guidanceText: For each risk, write what you do to reduce it, such as testing, human checks, or limits on use.

items.title: Record data quality and bias checks
items.guidanceText: Note where your data comes from and how you checked it for errors and bias.

templates.name: High-Risk AI Obligations
templates.description: The full set of duties that apply when an AI system is classified as high-risk. Deadlines: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems listed in Annex III, 2 August 2028 for AI in products covered by Annex I (moved from 2 August 2026 by the Digital Omnibus).

items.title: Maintain technical documentation
items.guidanceText: Confirm you keep documentation showing how the system was built and tested.

items.title: Provide clear instructions to operators
items.guidanceText: Describe the instructions and information you give to the people who run the system.

items.title: Set up human oversight
items.guidanceText: Name the person who can monitor and stop the system, and describe how they intervene.

items.title: Test accuracy, robustness and security
items.guidanceText: Summarise how you tested accuracy and protected the system against misuse and attacks.

items.title: Keep automatic logs
items.guidanceText: Confirm the system keeps logs of its operation so events can be traced.

templates.name: Transparency Obligations
templates.description: Duties for AI that interacts with people or generates content (limited-risk systems). Applies since 2 August 2026.

items.title: Tell users they are interacting with AI
items.guidanceText: Describe how you make clear to people that they are dealing with an AI, for example a chatbot notice.

items.title: Label AI-generated content
items.guidanceText: Explain how you label content the AI creates or changes, including synthetic media.

templates.name: Prohibited Practice Review
templates.description: This system may fall under a banned AI practice. Review and document urgently. The bans on AI that generates child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate images apply from 2 December 2026.

items.title: Confirm the system is not a banned practice
items.guidanceText: The classification suggests this system may be banned under Art. 5, for example social scoring or certain biometric uses. Document your review and get legal advice before any use.

requirements.title: Lawful basis for processing
requirements.guidanceText: Have a clear legal reason to use personal data in your AI, such as consent, a contract, or a legitimate interest. Write down which one you rely on.

requirements.title: Transparency and information
requirements.guidanceText: Tell people clearly how their data is used by the AI, in plain language, before or when you collect it.

requirements.title: Automated decisions and profiling
requirements.guidanceText: If the AI makes decisions about people with no human involved and a serious effect, you usually need extra safeguards, such as a right to human review.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.guidanceText: For high-risk AI processing, carry out a data protection impact assessment that describes the processing, the risks to people, and how you reduce them.

requirements.title: Data minimisation and accuracy
requirements.guidanceText: Use only the personal data you really need, keep it accurate, and do not keep it longer than necessary.

templates.name: GDPR Baseline for AI
templates.description: Core data protection steps for any AI that uses personal data.

items.title: Record your lawful basis
items.guidanceText: State the legal reason you use personal data in this AI system.

items.title: Document how you inform people
items.guidanceText: Describe the privacy information you give to the people whose data is used.

items.title: Assess automated decision making
items.guidanceText: Note whether the AI makes decisions about people on its own, and what safeguards you provide.

items.title: Complete a data protection impact assessment
items.guidanceText: If the processing is high risk, summarise your impact assessment and its outcome.

items.title: Apply data minimisation
items.guidanceText: Explain how you limit the personal data used and how long you keep it.

requirements.title: ICT and AI risk management framework
requirements.guidanceText: Put in place a documented framework to manage your technology and AI risks across the whole firm. The management body owns it and reviews it regularly.

requirements.title: Incident management and reporting
requirements.guidanceText: Detect, handle, classify and report major technology incidents to the competent authority within the set deadlines.

requirements.title: Digital resilience testing
requirements.guidanceText: Test the resilience of your critical technology and AI systems regularly, including advanced threat-led testing where it is required.

requirements.title: Third-party technology risk
requirements.guidanceText: Manage and document the risks from outside technology and AI providers, with key contract safeguards and a clear exit plan.

templates.name: DORA Operational Resilience
templates.description: Operational resilience steps for financial entities using technology and AI.

items.title: Document your ICT and AI risk management framework
items.guidanceText: Describe how you identify, manage and review technology and AI risks, and who owns it.

items.title: Set up incident detection and reporting
items.guidanceText: Explain how you detect, classify and report major ICT incidents on time.

items.title: Plan and run resilience testing
items.guidanceText: Describe your testing programme for critical systems.

items.title: Manage third-party providers and exit strategy
items.guidanceText: Record your key providers, contract safeguards and exit plan.

requirements.title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures
requirements.guidanceText: Adopt technical and organisational measures to manage the risks to your network and information systems, in proportion to the risk you face.

requirements.title: Management accountability
requirements.guidanceText: Your management body approves the cybersecurity measures, oversees them, and takes relevant training.

requirements.title: Incident reporting to the BSI
requirements.guidanceText: Report significant incidents to the BSI: an early warning within 24 hours, a notification within 72 hours, and a final report within one month.

requirements.title: Supply chain security
requirements.guidanceText: Address security in your supply chain and in your relationships with direct suppliers and service providers.

templates.name: NIS2 Cybersecurity Measures
templates.description: Cybersecurity duties for essential and important entities.

items.title: Implement risk-management measures
items.guidanceText: List the technical and organisational measures you have in place.

items.title: Get management approval and training
items.guidanceText: Record management sign-off and the training they received.

items.title: Set up incident reporting to the BSI
items.guidanceText: Describe your process and deadlines for reporting significant incidents.

items.title: Address supply-chain security
items.guidanceText: Explain how you assess and manage supplier security.

requirements.title: Access by design
requirements.guidanceText: Design connected products and related services so users can easily access the data they generate, by default and without undue effort.

requirements.title: Data sharing with third parties
requirements.guidanceText: On the user's request, make the generated data available to a third party under fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms.

requirements.title: No unfair contract terms
requirements.guidanceText: Do not impose unfair terms about data access and use on smaller businesses.

requirements.title: Cloud switching
requirements.guidanceText: Let customers switch cloud and edge services by removing obstacles and excessive charges.

templates.name: Data Act Compliance
templates.description: Fair data access and sharing for connected products and services.

items.title: Provide user access to product data
items.guidanceText: Describe how users can access the data their device or service produces.

items.title: Enable data sharing with third parties on request
items.guidanceText: Explain how you share data with a third party when the user asks.

items.title: Review contracts for unfair data terms
items.guidanceText: Note how you checked your contracts for unfair data clauses.

items.title: Support cloud switching
items.guidanceText: Describe how customers can move to another cloud or edge provider.

requirements.title: Secure by design
requirements.guidanceText: Design and build your product with digital elements to be secure, with no known exploitable vulnerabilities when you release it.

requirements.title: Vulnerability handling and updates
requirements.guidanceText: Identify, document and fix vulnerabilities, and provide security updates for the product's support period.

requirements.title: Report exploited vulnerabilities
requirements.guidanceText: Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents to the authority within the set deadlines.

requirements.title: Conformity assessment and CE marking
requirements.guidanceText: Carry out a conformity assessment and affix the CE marking before placing the product on the market.

templates.name: Cyber Resilience Act Compliance
templates.description: Cybersecurity duties for products with digital elements, including AI-enabled ones.

items.title: Apply secure-by-design requirements
items.guidanceText: Describe the security measures built into the product.

items.title: Set up vulnerability handling and updates
items.guidanceText: Explain how you find, fix and patch vulnerabilities over the support period.

items.title: Set up exploited-vulnerability reporting
items.guidanceText: Describe your process for reporting exploited vulnerabilities on time.

items.title: Complete conformity assessment and CE marking
items.guidanceText: Record your conformity assessment and CE marking.

requirements.title: Clear responsibility and governance
requirements.guidanceText: Keep clear human responsibility for AI-driven decisions. The management body stays accountable and cannot delegate this to the algorithm.

requirements.title: Data quality and bias
requirements.guidanceText: Use appropriate, representative data for your models and check for bias and data-quality problems.

requirements.title: Model validation
requirements.guidanceText: Validate models before you use them and re-validate them regularly, keeping documentation of the results.

requirements.title: Ongoing monitoring and human oversight
requirements.guidanceText: Continuously monitor model performance and keep meaningful human oversight of the outcomes.

templates.name: BaFin AI Governance
templates.description: BaFin's expectations for AI used by supervised financial firms.

items.title: Assign clear responsibility for AI decisions
items.guidanceText: Name who is accountable for the AI system and its decisions.

items.title: Document data quality and bias checks
items.guidanceText: Describe your data sources and how you checked them for quality and bias.

items.title: Validate and re-validate models
items.guidanceText: Summarise your validation approach and schedule.

items.title: Monitor performance and keep human oversight
items.guidanceText: Explain how you monitor the model and how a person oversees the outcomes.
